Connecticut Huskies.previous_hc_experience: Extensive at one place. The Coaching Carousel records Jason Candle at 81-44 at Toledo with no problems succeeding Matt Campbell, while noting the Rockets won the MAC only twice in 10 seasons under him and that he owns a career bowl record of 3-5. The team pages add that Candle's only stop outside Toledo was Division III Mount Union from 2003 to 2008.
Connecticut Huskies.oc: Nunzio Campanile, at Syracuse from 2023-25 and Rutgers before that. A co-coordinator and quarterbacks coach came from South Carolina.
Connecticut Huskies.dc: Ryan Manalac, a fellow Ohio native and Pitt's linebackers coach, who has never been an FBS coordinator. The guide describes him as a Pat Narduzzi disciple.
Connecticut Huskies.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Connecticut Huskies.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Connecticut Huskies.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Connecticut Huskies.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Connecticut Huskies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide's expectation is grounded in lineage and precedent: the defense has a good chance of being solid, since Manalac is a Pat Narduzzi disciple, and Toledo ranked second nationally in yards allowed per game and third in yards per play allowed.
Connecticut Huskies.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Connecticut Huskies.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide notes no clear starting quarterback and many position battles, with Toledo transfer Kalieb Osborne competing with Tennessee's Jake Merklinger and in-house options.
Connecticut Huskies.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 5 returning starters — a total of 0. The guide adds that under Candle, UConn ranks 138th in Phil Steele's Experience chart, and that with North Dakota State and Sacramento State now in FBS, 138th is officially dead last.
Connecticut Huskies.staff_turnover: Complete, and unusually so in composition. The guide observes that new head coaches normally bring assistants who know the scheme and the player types that fit it, then documents how little of that applies here: Campanile from Syracuse and Rutgers, Manalac from Pitt having never been an FBS coordinator, the special teams coordinator from Washington State, and the co-coordinator and quarterbacks coach from South Carolina. It applauds the diversity and nationwide recruiting connections while calling it surprising that a decade-long Toledo head coach has so many new colleagues.
Connecticut Huskies.prior_school: Toledo, though the guide identifies the specific shortfall: Candle brought some Toledo players so he is not starting with zero familiar faces, but none of his extremely productive offensive players followed, and only a couple on defense. It names K'Von Sherman, who had 93 tackles at Toledo, as the exception among recognisable transfers, along with Kalieb Osborne, Kenji Christian — at his fourth school, most recently Toledo — and three potential offensive line starters who were together at Toledo without playing much. Jim Mora Jr is the predecessor, having won 27 games in four seasons against the programme's 26 wins across 2012-21.
Connecticut Huskies.portal_recruiting: Extensive but unglamorous. The guide notes that even the transfers are largely not recognizable names.
Connecticut Huskies.vsin_assessment: A hire that looks great on the surface, with one specific and repeated reservation. The Coaching Carousel says on the surface this looks like a great hire given the 81-44 record, then qualifies it — Candle won the MAC only twice in 10 seasons, owns a 3-5 bowl record, and the Rockets have had a penchant for losing games as a big favorite, losing more than 10 times as a touchdown-or-more favorite from 2021-25. Its balance is situational: on the plus side he won't see a lot of big favorite roles with the Huskies; on the downside, a programme like UConn simply has to win games in which it is favored, and Candle has had major problems doing just that. The team pages call this a transitional, rebuilding year for both team and coach, admit the effect of leaving Toledo after 16 years is impossible to quantify, and separate the sides: the offense has major question marks, but the defense has a good chance of being solid.
Connecticut Huskies.strengths: A head coach at 81-44 over a decade who succeeded a highly regarded predecessor, a defensive coordinator from the Pat Narduzzi tree taking over a scheme lineage that produced the nation's second-best yards-allowed defense, a staff drawn from many programmes giving nationwide recruiting connections, and some familiar Toledo players including a 93-tackle linebacker.
Connecticut Huskies.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with five returning starters and last place nationally on Phil Steele's Experience chart, no clear starting quarterback and many position battles, none of Toledo's productive offensive players following, a defensive coordinator who has never held the role at FBS level, and a documented record of losing as a heavy favorite at a programme the guide says must win those games.
Connecticut Huskies.betting: The guide gives a genuinely two-sided answer on expectations: from 2021-25 Candle lost ten times as a touchdown-or-more favorite, so aiming low may suit a team that will rarely be favored with a completely new roster — while the Carousel's point is that a programme like UConn has to win the games in which it is favored. It closes on the bar UConn is falling from: 31.9 and 35.3 points per game the last two seasons and 6.7 yards per play last year, numbers it says the fan base probably will not see.
Connecticut Huskies.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens with the surface reading and then dismantles it. On the surface, this looks like a great hire: Candle went 81-44 at Toledo and had no problems succeeding Matt Campbell with the newfound success he brought to the Rockets. At the same time, he notes, Candle only won the MAC twice in 10 seasons as head coach and owns a career bowl record of 3-5 — not to mention the Rockets' penchant for losing games as a big favorite, losing more than 10 times as a TD-plus favorite from 2021-25. His balance is situational: on the plus side, Candle won't see a lot of big favorite roles with the Huskies; on the downside, a programme like UConn simply has to win games in which they are favored, and Candle has had major problems doing just that.

Notre Dame Fighting Irish.dc_status: Returning — Ash enters year two, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Notre Dame as one of 11 teams holding opponents under three yards per carry, with only eight allowing fewer yards per play, and notes that across seven years of coaching and personnel churn the programme has allowed more than 19.7 points per game only once, and under five yards per play in each of the last three seasons under Freeman.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records CJ Carr as not the running threat Riley Leonard was.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Carr's 24-to-6 ratio with three rushing scores, attributes his spring and summer as Heisman favorite substantially to the schedule, and flags that the depth behind him is a major worry if anything happens.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.continuity: Complete, and the highest in the guide. The Stability Score table (p. 43) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 4 for 17 returning starters — totalling 18.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.staff_turnover: None recorded. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning, and the guide notes the second-year defensive coordinator returns his top six tacklers.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.portal_recruiting: Addressed as retention. The guide offers a culture signal as evidence: the Irish were so aggrieved by the playoff snub that they skipped a bowl, and the only notable departures went to the NFL rather than to other schools.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.vsin_assessment: As close to unqualified as the guide gets. It records Freeman at 34-7 with a spectacular roster, answers its own questions about weaknesses on offense and defense with no in both cases, and calls a perfect season very attainable including the playoff provided cluster injuries are avoided. It flags one genuine caution — the Irish are +31 in turnover margin over two seasons, an area of concern unless Carr protects the ball — while expecting the ball-hawking to continue after 21 interceptions.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.strengths: The highest Stability Score in the guide at 18 with head coach, both coordinators and the quarterback all returning and 17 returning starters; a second-year defensive coordinator returning his top six tacklers; a seven-year record of allowing more than 19.7 points per game only once; a very good offensive line; and a retention picture in which the only notable departures went to the NFL.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.concerns: A quarterback who is not the running threat his predecessor was with major depth worries behind him, over 2,000 rushing yards and 29 scores to replace, only one notable returning receiver, and a +31 turnover margin over two seasons the guide flags as unlikely to be sustained.
Notre Dame Fighting Irish.betting: Projection is 11.42 wins, with Notre Dame favored by 8.5 or more in every game. The guide adds schedule mechanics as supporting detail: only four true road games at Purdue, North Carolina, BYU and Syracuse, two neutral-site games in Green Bay and Foxboro, and a well-timed bye giving an extra week to prepare for Navy's triple option after playing at elevation at BYU.
